clue.text: They can be disorderly for sure

definitions.text: They can be disorderly for sure

indicators.note: letters that can be disorderly may be thrown out of their order and reset in a new one

blocks.note: the two words taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A remark that certain people are, beyond doubt, prone to rowdiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the letters of 'for sure' in disorder spell the answer, and uproars are by nature disorderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Furores are outbursts of public uproar or commotion, which are typically chaotic and unruly.

clue.text: Point of Hamlet’s first appearance that could come as shock

indicators.note: first asks for just the opening letter of the word it is attached to

blocks.note: a head is a point of land jutting into the sea
taken as written
opening letter of the prince's name
an air is a manner or look someone has

explanation.surface: A theatre question about the moment the Prince of Denmark first walks on, which might startle the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like a jolt of surprise, but here it is a thick mass of hair: HEAD OF H AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is a thick, bushy mass of it on the scalp.

clue.text: My repeated appeal for attention that rapidly spreads

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'something that rapidly spreads'

blocks.note: the cry 'Me!' of someone wanting to be noticed
the same cry said again, as an eager child calls 'Me! Me!'

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that their own attention-seeking keeps going viral.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the eager shout 'Me! Me!' – a nod to the puzzle's theme of self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is an idea, image or joke passed rapidly from person to person, especially online.

clue.text: Sailed, having taken in small crew

indicators.note: having taken something in means holding it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: to boat is to travel by boat
S is the standard abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A yacht went out with only a skeleton crew aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew' looks like the sailors, but it is the past tense of crow.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to brag, so 'crew' as its past tense means bragged.

clue.text: Key individual like me, who can help with dislocation?

blocks.note: B is a musical key
one single person
the speaker is the puzzle's compiler, a crossword setter

explanation.surface: An important person, similar to the speaker, who might fix a displaced joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key individual' reads as one phrase meaning an important person; it splits into a musical key and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonesetter is a person, often unqualified, who resets broken bones and puts dislocated joints back in place.

clue.text: Finishes off this photograph to print another

definitions.note: stands for 'another photograph', echoing the photograph already named

indicators.note: the finishes of words are their final letters, so only the last of each is kept

blocks.note: last letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Instructions for completing a picture so that a fresh copy can be printed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'another' as 'another photograph': a shot is a picture, just like the one named in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is a photograph, so another photograph is another shot.

clue.text: Conclude in British article who’s responsible for this?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the following pair of pieces

blocks.note: BR is an abbreviation for British
to conclude is to finish
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A question about who is to blame, as if asking which British newspaper piece finished something.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the setter's own pseudonym: the person responsible for this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Brendan is the name under which this crossword's compiler publishes, so he is the person who made it.

clue.text: See group, oddly, as source of self-criticism

indicators.note: doing something oddly means doing it strangely, so the letters come out in an unusual order

blocks.note: the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to regard a social circle, strangely, as where one's self-doubt originates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' tempts a solver to take alternate letters, but it signals a rearrangement of the whole of 'See group'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freudian theory the superego is the part of the mind acting as conscience, judging and criticising the self.

clue.text: Not ourselves, and not herself – not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

blocks.note: the letters run from the second letter of the first word to inside the second

explanation.surface: A wry line about people being out of sorts, including one particular woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'not' makes the clue look like a list of negatives; the second 'not' is the start of the letter run.
explanation.definitionFit: Others are people apart from oneself or one's own group, so they are not us.

clue.text: Puzzle followed by two seconds without speaking

blocks.note: Wordle is the popular online daily word game
S is the abbreviation for second, taken twice

explanation.surface: Someone solves a puzzle in a couple of seconds and stays silent.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordle is a daily online five-letter guessing game, so it fits 'puzzle' exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordless means silent, not uttering any speech.

clue.text: For instance, consuming a container of food

definitions.text: For instance, consuming a container of food

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing something up, so the first piece holds the next inside it

blocks.note: e.g., for example
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: An example of a meal: someone working through a can of food.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: finishing a tin of food is an instance of the activity itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating is the act of taking food in, and polishing off a tin of something is one example of it.

clue.text: Errant life feels misrepresented, as is autobiography

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: describing what an autobiography is

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown in a false, distorted form, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the three words taken as written, fifteen letters

explanation.surface: Someone who has gone astray feels their memoir paints them falsely.
explanation.walkthrough: This entry names the puzzle's theme: many clues refer to themselves or to the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobiography is written about its own author, so it refers back to the self.

clue.text: For example, concert organized around one, considering nobody else

indicators.note: organized means put into a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered
around means the rearranged letters surround the following single piece

blocks.note: e.g., for example
taken as written, to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gig staged entirely around a single star who ignores everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concert' looks like the subject of the surface, but it is just a bag of letters; the Roman numeral for one sits inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Egocentric people think only of themselves and pay no regard to anyone else.

clue.text: Muscle problem to continue nursing? That’s right

blocks.note: to tend is to nurse or care for
on as in carry on, going further
'it is' agrees that something is correct

explanation.surface: A doctor asking whether a muscle injury means the patient needs more care, and being told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the inflammation affects a tendon rather than a muscle, but tendons attach muscles to bone, so the definition is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendonitis is inflammation of a tendon, the cord joining a muscle to bone, causing pain on movement.

clue.text: Important politician, one ranked moderately highly

blocks.note: first meaning: significant, of great size or consequence
a further meaning: John ..., UK Prime Minister 1990-97
second meaning: an army officer above captain and below lieutenant colonel

explanation.walkthrough: There are really three definitions: John Major was the British Prime Minister in the 1990s, and the rank sits in the middle of the officer ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adjective for significance, as a politician's surname, and as a military officer's rank.

clue.text: Inhibit action drawing attention to oneself

blocks.note: first meaning: to check or hold back growth
second meaning: a publicity-seeking act

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the verb, as stunted growth; the second is the noun, as a publicity exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: To stunt is to hamper development, and a stunt is a showy act done to gain notice.

clue.text: Revolutionary device that reproduces itself when up-ended

indicators.note: a word that is the same when turned upside down in a down entry reads identically from either end

blocks.note: a device that spins, whose letters read the same both ways; the setter uses the phrase twice on purpose

explanation.surface: A machine that turns, and somehow copies itself when flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics; here it simply means spinning round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is something that rotates, a device that turns about an axis.

clue.text: Keeping stone circle around another

indicators.note: around means the outer pieces enclose the single following one

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
a ring is a circle
another circle: the letter O is round

explanation.surface: Keeping a prehistoric stone circle surrounded by a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone circle' reads as one monument like Stonehenge, but it splits into a weight abbreviation and a ring; 'another' circle is the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Storing something means keeping it put away for later use.

clue.text: Peculiarity exemplified in what comes before and after

definitions.text: Peculiarity exemplified in what comes before and after

blocks.note: surface reading: some strangeness shown in what precedes and follows

blocks.clueFragment: exemplified in what comes before and after
blocks.note: setter's reading: the clue number 19 before and the enumeration 7 after are both odd numbers

explanation.surface: A strangeness shown in whatever comes before something and after it.
explanation.walkthrough: Another self-referring clue: look at the clue's own number (19) and its enumeration (7); both are odd.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer means peculiarity or strangeness, and it also describes odd numbers, which both flanking numbers are.

clue.text: Many folk find them foul

blocks.note: surface reading: lots of people think swear words are offensive
setter's reading: every word in the clue has exactly four letters

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is built entirely of words of the very length the answer names, so it describes itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Swear words are called this because so many common obscenities are short, crude words of that length.

clue.text: Left-winger that’s replaced extremes of Eastern philosopy

indicators.note: re-placed extremes are end letters put back in new positions, so the first and last letters change places

blocks.note: the Chinese philosophy of the Tao; the clue misspells 'philosophy'

explanation.surface: A communist who has abandoned the fringes of Oriental thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'replaced' as 're-placed': swap the outer letters of TAOISM to get MAOIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A Maoist follows the communist doctrine of Mao Zedong, so is politically on the far left.

clue.text: Like some setters, mostly kind of ornamental

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: the Irish setter is a breed of red gun dog

explanation.surface: Some compilers are a bit decorative in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setters' looks like crossword compilers in this setter-themed puzzle, but they are dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a flowering plant grown in gardens for decoration, an ornamental.

clue.text: Scattered in USSR as some of its people were

definitions.text: Scattered in USSR as some of its people were

indicators.note: scattered things are spread about in disarray, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: the three words taken as written

explanation.surface: A note that some Soviet citizens were dispersed across the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: many of these people were dispersed across the Soviet Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Russians were the largest nationality of the Soviet Union, living throughout its republics.

clue.text: One selfie’s border making American angry

indicators.note: a border is an edge, so only the outer letters of the word are kept
a border runs round what it frames, so the edge letters enclose the other piece

blocks.note: first and last letters of the photo word
an alternative, one or the other; the blog leaves this piece unexplained

explanation.surface: A single self-portrait photo whose frame infuriates a US viewer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sore means angry in American usage, hence the qualifier. The source of OR is uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English being sore means being annoyed or resentful.

clue.text: Thus cover the person writing in oblique symbols

blocks.note: so means thus, in this way
a lid is a cover
the setter, who is writing the clue, refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: An instruction to conceal the writer within slanting marks, like hiding behind punctuation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' looks like an instruction to wrap something, but it is simply a noun for a lid.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidi is the plural of solidus, the slash character used to separate items in text.

clue.text: Flowers from self-absorbed type? No way, ultimately

indicators.note: 'no' removes something and 'ultimately' says the removal happens at the very end of the word

blocks.note: someone obsessed with their own image
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Blooms produced by a vain person, in no way at all in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Narcissus, the youth in Greek myth who fell for his own reflection, became the flower, hence the link with self-absorption.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissi are the plural of narcissus, a genus of spring flowers including daffodils.
